# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vanLieshout_2026_bedaquiline"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vanLieshout_2026_bedaquiline"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70430> (open access; PMC13503988)

van Lieshout et al. (2026) did not fit a model to clinical data. They built a
forward prediction of the sputum early bactericidal activity (EBA) of
bedaquiline from two sources:

1. **Human PK**: the Svensson 2016 population PK model of bedaquiline and its
   metabolite M2, with its covariate effects (weight, age, Black race and a
   time-varying serum albumin) and its between-subject variability. Between-
   occasion variability was dropped. The same PK model is in this package as
   `Svensson_2016_bedaquiline`.
2. **Zebrafish PD**: an Emax exposure-response relationship for bedaquiline
   against *Mycobacterium marinum* in zebrafish larvae (Forn-Cuni et al. 2026).
   Its EC50 of 26.5 mg/L (whole-body concentration) was scaled to humans by the
   ratio of the bedaquiline MICs for *M. tuberculosis* and *M. marinum*
   (Equation 1). Its maximum effect, 109% of the *M. marinum* growth rate
   constant (0.0853 1/h) and then 137%, became the maximum kill rate. Net
   growth of *M. tuberculosis* was set to zero.

They compared the predictions with two phase 2a trials, Rustomjee 2008 (7 days,
aggregate data) and Diacon 2013 (14 days, individual data from TB-PACTS).
Supplementary Materials give the full NONMEM simulation code, and every value in
the packaged model is taken from that code.

# Population

The predictions target adults with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis who had
not received bedaquiline before, in two randomised, double-blind,
placebo-controlled phase 2a EBA trials:

* **Rustomjee 2008**: 45 participants, 25, 100 or 400 mg once daily for
  7 days.
* **Diacon 2013**: 60 participants. Each arm had two loading doses and then a
  daily maintenance dose: 200/100/100, 400/300/200, 500/400/300 or
  700/500/400 mg (day 1 / day 2 / day 3 onward). The arms are labelled by the
  maintenance dose (100-400 mg).

The paper does not tabulate demographics for either trial. The PK model was
developed in 335 patients with MDR-TB (Svensson 2016).

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("vanLieshout_2026_bedaquiline")()$population)
```

# Source trace

All `$THETA` values are `FIX` in the Supplementary Materials model code. The
code's own comments trace THETA(9)-THETA(24) to Svensson 2016 Table 3.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lmat` (MAT) | 6 x 0.662045 = 3.972 h | Model code THETA(9); `MAT = 6*EXP(PHI)/(EXP(PHI)+1)` with IOV = 0 |
| `fr` | 0.466443 | THETA(10) |
| `lcl`, `lvc` | 2.61592 L/h, 198.34 L | THETA(11), THETA(12) |
| `lq`, `lvp` | 3.658 L/h, 8549.06 L | THETA(13), THETA(14) |
| `lq2`, `lvp2` | 7.33504 L/h, 2690.91 L | THETA(15), THETA(16) |
| `lcl_m2`, `lvc_m2` | 10.0496 L/h, 2203.71 L | THETA(17), THETA(18) |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.180912, 1 | THETA(19), THETA(20); reference weight 70 kg |
| `e_alb_vc` | 1 | THETA(21), unbound-fraction effect on the observation volumes |
| `e_alb_cl` | 1.64021 | THETA(22) |
| `e_race_black_cl` | 0.838743 | THETA(23) |
| `e_age_cl` | 0.00880756 /year | THETA(24); `AGECL = 1 + (32-AGE)*THETA(24)` |
| `lalb0`, `lalb_ss` | 3.64865, 4.04068 g/dL | THETA(1), THETA(2) |
| `lkrep_alb` | 0.03399109 /week | THETA(3) |
| `bc_alb0`, `bc_alb_ss` | -2.43936, -5.37749 | THETA(4), THETA(5) (Box-Cox shapes) |
| `lkg_mm` | 0.0853 /h | `GROWTH_Mm`; Methods, 'Translational predictions' |
| `kg` | 0 | `GROWTH_MTB` |
| `f_emax_kg`, `f_emax_kg_late` | 1.09, 1.37 | `EMAX_BASE`, `IF(T.GT.72) EMAX_BASE = 1.37` |
| `t_emax_switch` | 72 h | `IF(T.GT.72)` |
| `lec50_zf` | 26.5 mg/L | `BDQ_EC50 = 26.5 * (...)`; Methods |
| `mic_mtb`, `mic_mm` | 0.04145085, 0.1 mg/L | `MIC_MTB_TARGET`, `MIC_Mm_ORIGIN` |
| `hill` | 1 | `BDQ_GAMMA` |
| `etalalb0 + etalalb_ss + etalkrep_alb` | block | `$OMEGA BLOCK(5)` elements 1-3 |
| `etalfdepot` | 0.0803271 | `$OMEGA` 10 |
| `etalcl + etalcl_m2` | 0.152776, 0.13486, 0.212124 | `$OMEGA BLOCK(2)` 11-12 |
| `etalvc`, `etalq`, `etalvc_m2` | 0.171909, 0.181182, 0.150223 | `$OMEGA` 13-15 |
| `expSd`, `expSd_m2` | sqrt(0.0518161), sqrt(0.0366836) | `$SIGMA BLOCK(2)` diagonal |
| Albumin trajectory | `ALB(t) = Xss / (1 + (Xss/X0 - 1) exp(-krep t))` | Closed form of `DADT(8)` |
| PK ODEs | 2 transits, 3-cmt BDQ, 1-cmt M2 | `DADT(1)`-`DADT(7)` |
| Kill rate | `Emax C / (C + EC50)`, `C = A(2)/V` | `BDQ_EFFECT` in `$DES` |
| Bacterial load | `d cfu/dt = kg cfu - kill cfu`, `cfu(0) = 10^baseline` | `DADT(9)`, `A_0(9)` |
| Observation volumes | `V * (Xss_pop/ALB)^1` | `VE`, `VM2E` in `$ERROR` |

## Translation constants

Equation 1 and the Methods give the human EC50 and the maximum kill rate
("0.093-0.117 h-1") directly. The packaged parameters reproduce them exactly:

```{r constants}
mod <- readModelDb("vanLieshout_2026_bedaquiline")
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
p <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)
ec50_human <- exp(p[["lec50_zf"]]) * p[["mic_mtb"]] / p[["mic_mm"]]
emax_early <- p[["f_emax_kg"]] * exp(p[["lkg_mm"]])
emax_late <- p[["f_emax_kg_late"]] * exp(p[["lkg_mm"]])
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Quantity = c("Human EC50 (mg/L)", "Emax, t <= 72 h (1/h)", "Emax, t > 72 h (1/h)"),
    Packaged = signif(c(ec50_human, emax_early, emax_late), 4),
    Paper = c("26.5 x 0.0415 / 0.1", "0.093", "0.117")
  )
)
stopifnot(
  abs(ec50_human - 26.5 * 0.04145085 / 0.1) < 1e-9,
  abs(emax_early - 0.093) < 0.0005,
  abs(emax_late - 0.117) < 0.0005
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The 14-day predictions used each participant's own covariates and the
7-day predictions used study means. Neither set is published, so every
simulated participant here has the median weight (56 kg, between the 55 and
57 kg stage medians of the Svensson 2016 cohort), the reference age of 32 years
and non-Black race. The baseline bacterial load is set to each regimen's
published mean (Results, 'Simulated exposures and baselines'). Each arm has 200
participants, and the PK parameters vary through the model's between-subject
variability.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study,           ~arm,     ~d1, ~d2, ~dm, ~ndose, ~bl,
  "Diacon 2013",    "100 mg", 200, 100, 100, 14,     5.96,
  "Diacon 2013",    "200 mg", 400, 300, 200, 14,     5.69,
  "Diacon 2013",    "300 mg", 500, 400, 300, 14,     5.82,
  "Diacon 2013",    "400 mg", 700, 500, 400, 14,     6.20,
  "Rustomjee 2008", "25 mg",  25,  25,  25,  7,      6.66,
  "Rustomjee 2008", "100 mg", 100, 100, 100, 7,      6.32,
  "Rustomjee 2008", "400 mg", 400, 400, 400, 7,      6.82
) |>
  mutate(group = paste(study, arm, sep = ", "))

n_per_arm <- 200
make_arm <- function(k) {
  a <- arms[k, ]
  ids <- (k - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  amts <- c(a$d1, a$d2, rep(a$dm, a$ndose - 2))
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, dose_no = seq_len(a$ndose)) |>
    mutate(time = (dose_no - 1) * 24, amt = amts[dose_no], evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_) |>
    select(-dose_no)
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, a$ndose * 24, by = 24), seq(144, 168, by = 1))))
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(
      WT = 56, AGE = 32, RACE_BLACK = 0,
      SPUTUM_BL_LOG10CFU = a$bl,
      study = a$study, arm = a$arm, group = a$group
    )
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), make_arm)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("study", "arm", "group"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: bacterial burden over time

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 1 of van Lieshout 2026: median and 95% prediction interval
# of log10 CFU/mL by treatment arm.
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(time %% 24 == 0) |>
  group_by(study, arm, group, day = time / 24) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(log_cfu, 0.025),
    med = median(log_cfu),
    hi = quantile(log_cfu, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = arms$group))
ggplot(vpc, aes(day, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(linetype = "dashed", colour = "navy") +
  facet_wrap(~group, nrow = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 8)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since start of treatment (days)",
    y = "Bacterial burden (log10 CFU/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of van Lieshout 2026 (baseline fixed at the regimen mean)."
  )
```

The ribbons are narrower than the published ones at day 0. Here every
participant in an arm starts at the regimen mean, while the published
intervals also spread over the individual (14-day study) or simulated (7-day
study) baselines. The decline over time is what the model predicts, and the
EBA comparison below checks it directly.

## Figure 2a: EBA0-14d

Killing is first order in the bacterial load, so the EBA,
log10 CFU(day 0) - log10 CFU(day 14), does not depend on the baseline. That
makes it the cleanest quantitative check against the paper. The text reports
the 95% prediction interval for each 14-day arm.

```{r eba-baseline-free}
# Same typical participant, two different baselines: identical EBA.
ev_bl <- events |>
  filter(id == 3 * n_per_arm + 1) |>
  mutate(id = 1L)
eba_typ <- sapply(c(4, 8), function(bl) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
    events = mutate(ev_bl, SPUTUM_BL_LOG10CFU = bl),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  s$log_cfu[s$time == 0][1] - s$log_cfu[s$time == 336][1]
})
eba_typ
stopifnot(abs(diff(eba_typ)) < 1e-6)
```

```{r figure-2a}
eba <- sim |>
  filter(study == "Diacon 2013", time %in% c(0, 336)) |>
  group_by(id, arm) |>
  summarise(eba = log_cfu[time == 0][1] - log_cfu[time == 336][1], .groups = "drop")

published_eba <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,     ~obs_mean, ~pi_lo, ~pi_hi,
  "100 mg", 0.828,     0.287,  1.09,
  "200 mg", 0.975,     0.595,  2.05,
  "300 mg", 1.18,      0.825,  2.81,
  "400 mg", 1.61,      1.12,   3.61
)
eba_cmp <- eba |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    sim_med = median(eba),
    sim_lo = quantile(eba, 0.025),
    sim_hi = quantile(eba, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(published_eba, by = "arm")

eba_cmp |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Arm (maintenance dose)" = arm,
    "Simulated median" = sim_med,
    "Simulated 2.5%" = sim_lo,
    "Simulated 97.5%" = sim_hi,
    "Observed mean" = obs_mean,
    "Published 2.5%" = pi_lo,
    "Published 97.5%" = pi_hi
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "EBA0-14d (log10 CFU/mL): simulated versus the published 95% prediction interval (Results).")

ggplot(eba, aes(arm, eba)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "navy", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = published_eba,
    aes(x = arm, ymin = pi_lo, ymax = pi_hi),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "darkorange", width = 0.3, linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = published_eba, aes(x = arm, y = obs_mean),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "darkorange", size = 3
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Daily bedaquiline dose (Diacon 2013 arm)",
    y = "EBA0-14d (log10 CFU/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Violins: simulated. Orange: published 95% PI and observed mean.",
      "Replicates Figure 2a of van Lieshout 2026."
    )
  )

pct_bounds <- with(eba_cmp, 100 * c((sim_lo - pi_lo) / pi_lo, (sim_hi - pi_hi) / pi_hi))
stopifnot(
  # The simulated median lies inside every published 95% PI.
  all(eba_cmp$sim_med > eba_cmp$pi_lo & eba_cmp$sim_med < eba_cmp$pi_hi),
  # Envelope: a mis-transcribed EC50, MIC ratio or Emax moves every
  # interval by tens of percent.
  median(abs(pct_bounds)) < 20
)
```

The simulated intervals agree closely with the published ones, which also
include spread from the participants' own covariates. The median EBA rises
from about 0.6 to 2.2 log10 CFU/mL from the 100 mg arm to the 400 mg arm. The
observed mean in the 400 mg arm (1.61) sits below the predicted median, the
"slight overprediction of the drug effect in the highest dosing group" that the
paper reports.

# PKNCA validation

Supplementary Figure S1B shows the simulated median bedaquiline concentration
over the seventh dosing interval (144-168 h) of the 7-day study. The table
compares Cmax and the end-of-interval concentration with values the
maintainers digitised from that figure. Those are medians of the authors' own
simulation and not observed data.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(study == "Rustomjee 2008", time >= 144, time <= 168, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  transmute(id, time, conc = Cc * 1000, treatment = arm)

dose_nca <- events |>
  filter(study == "Rustomjee 2008", evid == 1, time == 144) |>
  transmute(id, time, amt, treatment = arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 144, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, clast.obs = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

# Digitised medians from Supplementary Figure S1B (log10 axis, ng/mL).
published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~clast.obs,
  "25 mg",    132,   39,
  "100 mg",   531,   157,
  "400 mg",   2138,  646
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "clast.obs"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", clast.obs = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Day 7 (144-168 h) bedaquiline exposure: simulated median versus Supplementary Figure S1B. * differs by >20%."
)

cmax_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(cmax = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(published_nca, treatment, ref = cmax), by = "treatment")
stopifnot(abs(median(100 * (cmax_sim$cmax - cmax_sim$ref) / cmax_sim$ref)) < 25)
```

Cmax agrees with the figure to within about 6%. The end-of-interval
concentration is 8-13% higher than the digitised medians. That is within what
the assumed covariates (the trial's demographics are not reported, and Black
race raises clearance by 84%) and reading values off a log axis can explain.

```{r pk-profile}
sim |>
  filter(study == "Rustomjee 2008", time >= 144, time <= 168) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.025) * 1000,
    med = median(Cc) * 1000,
    hi = quantile(Cc, 0.975) * 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = c("25 mg", "100 mg", "400 mg"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)",
    y = "Bedaquiline plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Daily dose", fill = "Daily dose",
    caption = "Replicates Supplementary Figure S1B of van Lieshout 2026."
  )
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariates.** The paper used individual covariates for the 14-day study and
  study means for the 7-day study, but publishes neither. The virtual cohort
  gives every participant 56 kg, 32 years and non-Black race.
* **Baseline bacterial load** is a covariate (`SPUTUM_BL_LOG10CFU`), as in the
  model code (`A_0(9) = 10**BASELINE`). The paper derived it from the clinical
  data: individual empirical Bayes estimates from an intercept model for the
  14-day study, and values simulated from the regimen means and pooled variance
  for the 7-day study. The intercept model itself is not published. The
  vignette uses the regimen means. The EBA does not depend on this choice.
* **Emax switch time.** The Methods say the maximum effect "increased to 137%
  after 24 hours of BDQ exposure" in zebrafish. The model code applies the
  switch when the simulation time exceeds 72 h (`IF(T.GT.72)`), and the packaged
  model follows the code. The switch is on absolute time `t`, so the first
  bedaquiline dose must be given at `t = 0`.
* **Albumin.** The code integrates a logistic albumin ODE from `t = 0`. The
  packaged model uses its exact closed-form solution, so it has no extra state.
  The albumin observation and its residual error (`$SIGMA` 1) are not included
  as an output.
* **Weight.** The Svensson 2016 weight-trajectory model is legacy code in the
  supplement ("disabled for simulations"). Its parameters, THETA(6)-THETA(8)
  and `$OMEGA` elements 4-5, are not carried, and the subject's `WT` is used
  directly, as in the code.
* **Between-occasion variability** on F and MAT is `0 FIX` in the code and is
  omitted.
* **Residual error.** The code's between-subject variability on the residual
  error (`IIV_RUV1`, `IIV_RUV2`) and the BDQ-M2 residual covariance are not
  carried. The log-scale additive errors are kept as independent `lnorm()`
  terms. The bacterial load has no residual error ("0 RUV for bacteria").
* **Sensitivity analyses.** The two alternative translational factors in the
  supplement (allometric zebrafish central volume, whole-body human
  concentration) predicted worse and are not part of the packaged model.
